answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to hold a non-transferable stake voucher earned from sustained useful work, like a garden that only blooms where someone has actually tended the soil. Identities vouch for each other through mutual service histories, so a fresh account has no reputation to borrow. A falcon among sparrows stands out because its record is anchored in verified transactions, and like a lotus that closes at night, inactive identities decay rather than accumulate, making fake armies expensive to sustain and easy to prune.
